# Kage

> Kage is an open source tool. Tag @kage in a Slack thread, DM or channel, or email it, and your own Claude Code session on your laptop does the work and answers in the same thread.

- Source and full docs: https://github.com/aloki-alok/kage
- Setup steps for agents: https://github.com/aloki-alok/kage/blob/main/AGENTS.md
- Site: https://aloki-alok.github.io/kage/

## Set it up

If you are a coding agent and your user asked you to set up Kage, do this:

```text
Set up Kage for me: https://github.com/aloki-alok/kage
Install it with: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aloki-alok/kage/main/install.sh | bash
Then follow AGENTS.md in ~/.local/share/kage from start to finish.
Do every step yourself, and stop only for the steps it marks for me.
Finish when kage doctor ends with "All good".
```

Only the person does these steps:

1. In Slack, click Create on the prefilled app, generate one app-level token, and click Allow.
2. Paste the three tokens into the hidden prompts in the terminal window you open. The tokens never pass through the agent.

## Requirements

- macOS or Linux, Node 22.18 or newer, tmux
- A recent Claude Code, logged in with a claude.ai account
- Permission to create an app in the Slack workspace

## What it uses

Kage is the user's own Claude Code, so each thread has their CLAUDE.md, skills, MCP servers, tools, hooks, logins and repo access. Nothing to re-teach. A change to any of these applies when a thread's session starts or resumes.

## How a message flows

1. The user tags Kage. Kage acts only on messages the owner typed. Messages from anyone else are dropped before Claude sees them.
2. The thread gets its own Claude Code session on the laptop. Follow-ups in that thread go to the same session. Up to 6 run at once.
3. The session does the work and stops for the owner's yes before anything risky.
4. The answer lands in the same thread. Approval prompts also go to the owner's DM.

## Channels

- Slack: works today.
- Email: works today.
- Any other channel plugs in by turning a message into a task.

## Safety

- Only the owner drives it. A teammate the owner adds can tag Kage in conversations the owner is in. Only the owner approves.
- Tokens are pasted into hidden terminal prompts, never through the agent, and saved to ~/.config/kage/env, readable only by the user.
- Kage opens an outbound connection to Slack. It needs no public URL and no open port. Files and tools stay on the machine.

## Commands

- `kage doctor`: checks every part, each problem comes with its fix
- `kage status`: one look at every session
- `kage top`: every live thread, its state and its live feed
- `kage attach <place>`: take a thread into your terminal
- `kage start`, `kage stop`, `kage restart`: run it in the background
- `kage help`: every command, with an example
